title: Evidence Flow Runner - implementation and runbook
body:
Purpose
This note defines the Evidence Flow Runner: an operational component that automates collection, normalization, packaging, and delivery of control evidence from Redwood systems into long-term evidence stores and SIEMs. The goal is to make control evidence reproducible, auditable, and tamper-evident for internal audits and external compliance reviews (SOC2, ISO27001, GDPR controls mapping).

Scope
- Ingest sources: RBAC v2 events, API audit logs (hosted API + dedicated control plane), infra-level events (k8s/audit), console actions, and evidence artifacts produced by other automation (e.g., infra-as-code deploy records).
- Normalization: map incoming payloads to the internal audit schema v2 (see schema section).
- Evidence packaging: attach control mapping metadata, compute cryptographic fingerprints, and store human-readable summaries + raw payloads.
- Delivery: forward minimal enriched events to SIEM exporters (Splunk/Datadog/QRadar), and persist full packages in the Evidence Store (S3-compatible bucket with lifecycle + immutability options).
- Workflow orchestration: retries, deduplication, attestations, and manual review handoffs.

Non-goals
- This runner is not a full replacement for real-time monitoring agents that feed metrics/alerts (Prometheus). It focuses on evidence fidelity and compliance workflows rather than production observability.

High-level design
1) Source adapters: lightweight collectors run as either sidecar or central ingestion services. Collectors should support both pull and push modes: push from services via HTTPS (mutual TLS) or push from audit log exporters; pull from message buses (Kafka/PubSub) or directly from object stores for batch exports.
2) Normalizer: stateless lambda-like service that validates event schema, enriches with context (actor identity from RBAC v2, org/team tags), and assigns control IDs (example: CTRL-RBAC-01 -> role-change evidence).
3) Evidence Packager: bundles raw event(s), normalized JSON, derived metadata (control_ids[], timewindow, root_hash), and an HTML/markdown auditor summary. Produces an immutable tar.gz with accompanying metadata.json and signature.
4) Evidence Store: S3 with server-side encryption (SSE-KMS) + object lock for retention/immutability when required by control. Each package path: evidence/{org}/{control_id}/{YYYY}/{MM}/{sha256}.tar.gz
5) SIEM Exporter: publishes a lightweight event representing "evidence produced" plus key attributes to a SIEM ingestion endpoint. Full payloads are not streamed to SIEM to limit egress/cost; link to Evidence Store + PGP signed manifest is provided.
6) Orchestrator: durable workflow (Temporal) to manage retries, backoff, manual approvals, and cross-service transactions (e.g., wait for signature issuance from KMS HSM).

Audit schema v2 (summary)
- top-level fields: id, source, source_id, timestamp_utc, event_type, actor {id, type, principal_type}, target {resource_id, resource_type}, raw_payload_url, normalized_payload, control_ids (list), derived_tags (list), schema_version: "audit_v2-2025-11"
- schema versioning: normalizer must include schema_version and maintain backwards-compatible parsers for v1 and v1.1 when migrating.

RBAC v2 specifics
- RBAC v2 emits role_change and binding_change events. Normalizer must canonicalize actor identities (SAML/SCIM/Okta/SSO user ids -> internal principal_id) using the identity service cache.
- Control mapping example: role_change -> CTRL-RBAC-03 (separation of duties), binding_change with service account -> CTRL-RBAC-07 (service account escalation).
- For role changes, include pre-image and post-image diffs; include timestamped policy versions.

Integrity and attestations
- Each evidence package MUST be hashed and signed. Signing flow:
  1) Package created and tarballed.
  2) Compute sha256 and store as metadata.
  3) Submit package hash to KMS signing service (HSM-backed) and attach signature to metadata.json.
  4) Store signature in Evidence Store and publish a minimal proof record to SIEM exporter containing {package_path, sha256, signature_key_id}.
- Rotation: signing key metadata must be attached with key ID and rotation epoch. Audits will need mapping from key_id -> certificate chain stored in key-management catalog.

Delivery guarantees and idempotency
- Exactly-once semantics desired from orchestrator perspective. Achieve by dedup table (DynamoDB/Cloud Spanner): key=source+source_id+ingest_window_hash -> evidence_package_id. If duplicate detected, orchestrator links to existing package.
- Retries: exponential backoff with jitter and circuit-breaker to prevent hot-looping from noisy sources.
- Poison messages: move to quarantine bucket and create an investigation ticket (auto-create JIRA ticket JIRA-SC-POISON-YYYYMMDD).

SIEM export format and batching
- Exporter sends batched events (size-limited) to SIEM via HTTPS with mutual TLS. Payload fields: evidence_id, control_ids, event_count, sample_events (truncated), evidence_store_url, sha256, signature_key_id, produced_at.
- Maintain a per-org rate limit to prevent noisy tenants from flooding SIEM.
- Exporter supports both push (webhook) and pull (SIEM can query an authenticated endpoint for new evidence pointers).

Operational runbook (high level)
- Normal failures: missing identity enrichment -> mark as "identity_pending" and requeue for enrichment after identity cache refresh.
- Evidence stuck in packaging -> runakia: check s3 temp-staging permissions, KMS signing availability, orchestrator worker logs.
- SIEM delivery failures -> exporter retries; if persistent (24h), mark as "siem_retry_pending" and notify CS/eng on-call.
- Quarantine handling: security reviewer triages and either reprocesses (after fixing schema) or marks evidence as irrecoverable and provides a manual attestation.

Testing & verification
- Unit tests for normalizer: mapping RBAC events, diff coverage for role changes, and schema conformance tests using generated fixtures.
- Integration: end-to-end test harness that simulates RBAC v2 events, verifies packaging, signature enrichment (use test KMS), upload to test Evidence Store, and mock SIEM ingestion receiver.
- Fuzzing: random payload injection to validate dedup and poison handling.

Privacy & redaction
- Sensitive fields (PII) must be redacted or tokenized when not required by control. Normalizer will apply per-control redaction policy. Example policy: CTRL-AUTH-05 requires user email redacted to hashed-email, but user_id preserved.
- Redaction logs must be kept alongside evidence to show what was removed and why (useful during audits).

Data retention and lifecycle
- Evidence retention controlled by control mapping: default retention 7 years for high-risk controls, 1 year for low-risk. Evidence Store lifecycle rules implement expiration and cold storage transitions. For immutable retention (legal hold), enable S3 Object Lock mode for that object prefix.

Operational metrics and dashboards
- Metrics: ingestion rate, packaging latency P50/P95/P99, signer latency, SIEM export success rate, dedupe rate, quarantine rate.
- Alerts: packaging error rate > 1% for 15m, signer latency 99th > 60s, SIEM failure rate >10% for 1h.

Open questions / TODOs
- Do we need to store full raw payloads for all controls or only for high/medium-severity controls? (security/Legal to decide.)
- Confirm per-tenant rate limiting and cost allocation model for SIEM forwarding. (Billing/product)
- Finalize key rotation policy (rotation frequency vs audit re-signing requirements). (sec/infra)
- Decide whether to use Temporal or StepFunctions for orchestrator (Temporal preferred by infra but requires infra investment).

Appendices
- Quick mapping example: RBAC event -> control ids -> example evidence path
  Event: binding_change: user: U123 removed from role: role-admin at 2025-11-03T14:23Z
  Normalized: {id: evt-9876, source: rbac-v2, timestamp_utc: ...}
  Control IDs: [CTRL-RBAC-03, CTRL-ACCESS-02]
  Package path: evidence/acme-corp/CTRL-RBAC-03/2025/11/3/0b12f9...tar.gz

- Minimal acceptance criteria for MVP
  * Collectors for RBAC v2 + API audit logs implemented
  * Normalizer with audit_schema_v2 validation
  * Evidence packaging and KMS-signed manifests stored in test Evidence Store
  * SIEM exporter that publishes pointer events to Splunk test instance
  * End-to-end integration tests and runbook steps documented

Notes to reviewers
- This is a working draft. Focus review on control mapping accuracy (sec), schema completeness (platform), and signing/retention constraints (infra/legal). Leave inline comments in the Confluence design page or ping in #security-architecture.

Changelog
- 2025-11-04: initial draft by Aisha Kapoor
- 2025-11-12: added signing flow and packaging format (Ben Chu)
- 2025-11-18: updated retention + SIEM export options (Marta Alvarez)
